newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Telecom seeks clarification on Taiwan bid.
newsitem.headline: HK Telecom seeks clarification on Taiwan bid.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd said on Friday it was seeking clarification of newspaper reports that Taiwan was blocking its participation in the bidding process for a mobile phone licence because of its China shareholder base.
"We are contacting Taiwan authorities for clarification of the news reports," the company's manager of media relations, Louis Liu, told Reuters.

Hong Kong newspapers said a Taiwanese telecommunications official was reported as saying Hongkong Telecom would be forced to sell its stake in a consortium bidding for the licences because its shareholder base included mainland Chinese investors.
Hong Kong-listed CITIC Pacific Ltd, controlled by China's state trading giant China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC), holds about eight percent of Hongkong Telecom.
The Hongkong Telecom spokesman said the company had not heard of any blocking of bids made by Taishiu Telecom Corp, a consortium in which Hong Kong Telecom owns a 15 percent stake.
Taishiu is bidding for two separate licences to provide Personal Communications Services (PCS) and GSM mobile telephone services in northern Taiwan.
The Taiwanese government said in October it had received 42 applications from 17 joint ventures for eight mobile phone operating licences.
According to the initial programme, successful bidders would be announced on January 4, Liu said, adding he was not sure whether the tender results would be announced on schedule.
"Everything seems to be so uncertain," he said.

Hongkong Telecom also holds 26 percent of privately held Taiwan Telecommunications Network Services (TTNS), which aims to become a full service provider once Taiwan's telcommunications industry is fully deregulated.
